showcase-grace-lp6-plan.html:
LP6 · Grace · Second conditional and the essay plan

LESSON AT A GLANCE

Last time: relative clauses; “whose” still shaky.

Today: second conditional for arguments (“If schools banned phones, …”), a Grammar Auction, linkers flash cards, and planning the HW6 opinion essay.

BEFORE CLASS

Laptop — Lesson Games: “Second Conditional Auction” · “If I Were Builder” · “Linkers Flash Cards”

SEGMENT 0 — WARM-UP (~8 min, 20:00–20:08)

0A · Who / which / whose (8 min, 20:00–20:08)

Rules. Say: “Finish my sentence: That’s the girl whose…” Three each way.

Key

whose + noun (whose bag) · who for people · which for things

SEGMENT 1 — GRAMMAR: SECOND CONDITIONAL (~20 min, 20:08–20:28)

Material: Lesson Games “Second Conditional Auction”, “If I Were Builder” — her screen

1A · Present (8 min, 20:08–20:16)

Present. Type: “If I had more time, I would read more.” Ask: “Do I have more time?” → no. “So is this real or imagined?” → imagined.

Rule, word for word: “If + past, would + base verb. It’s about now, but not real.”

  • ⚠ TRAP (would in both halves)
  • Spring: “Finish it: If schools banned phones…”
  • Right: “…students would talk more.”
  • Expect: “If schools would ban phones, …”
  • Repair: “No would after if.” Wait.

1B · Second Conditional Auction (6 min, 20:16–20:22)

Open Lesson Games “Second Conditional Auction”.

1C · If I Were Builder (6 min, 20:22–20:28)

Open Lesson Games “If I Were Builder”.

SEGMENT 2 — ESSAY PLAN (~26 min, 20:28–20:54)

Material: Lesson Games “Linkers Flash Cards” — her screen · the shared doc

2A · Linkers Flash Cards (6 min, 20:28–20:34)

Open Lesson Games “Linkers Flash Cards”.

2B · Plan the essay (20 min, 20:34–20:54)

Rules. In the shared doc: opinion, two reasons, one counter-argument. She writes; you ask “Why?” after each reason.

SEGMENT 3 — CLOSE (~4 min, 20:54–20:58)

3A · Homework HW6 (4 min, 20:54–20:58)

Say: “HW6: the grammar sheet, then the essay, 180 words, using your plan.”

BUFFER (~2 min, 20:58–21:00)

Overrun only.

PLANNING RECORD

Main: second conditional.

Next: LP7 — HW6 back; despite / although.

showcase-grace-lp7-plan.html:
LP7 · Grace · Contrast linkers in an opinion essay

LESSON AT A GLANCE

Last time: second conditional and the essay plan. HW6 set: a grammar sheet (linkers) and a 180-word opinion essay, “Should phones be allowed at school?”.

Today: both parts of HW6 back, despite / although (she has missed “despite” in three lessons), an error auction, rewriting her weakest paragraph, and a Tower Defence break.

Online: her essay is in the shared doc; the games go on her screen through the class link.

BEFORE CLASS

Laptop — Lesson Games: “Linkers Match Up” · “Despite or Although Quiz” · “Error Auction” · “Conditionals Builder” · “Tower Defence”

Her HW6 essay open in the shared doc, with your comments hidden until 2B.

SEGMENT 0 — HOMEWORK BACK (~14 min, 20:00–20:14)

0A · HW6 grammar sheet (6 min, 20:00–20:06)

Rules. She reads her answer; you say only “yes” or “look again”. She fixes it herself.

Key — HW6 grammar sheet (linkers, from HW6’s key page)

Pt1: 1 although · 2 despite · 3 However · 4 whereas · 5 In spite of · 6 Even though

Pt2: 1 Despite the rain, we played. · 2 Although it rained, we played. · 3 It rained. However, we played.

Watch: “despite of”, “although of”, “despite it rained”.

0B · HW6 essay (8 min, 20:06–20:14)

Rules. Scroll the shared doc. Ask: “Which paragraph are you least happy with?” Then go through the checklist with her paragraph by paragraph.

Key — HW6 essay checklist

1 Clear opinion in the first paragraph · 2 One reason per body paragraph · 3 At least two contrast linkers, used correctly · 4 A counter-argument and a reply · 5 Conclusion repeats the opinion in new words · 6 160–200 words

Done when: both keys checked; she has chosen one paragraph to rewrite in 2B.

SEGMENT 1 — GRAMMAR: DESPITE / ALTHOUGH (~16 min, 20:14–20:30)

Material: Lesson Games “Linkers Match Up”, “Despite or Although Quiz” — her screen

1A · Present the difference (6 min, 20:14–20:20)

Present. Type two sentences in the chat and ask what comes after each linker:

Although it was late, she kept working. → a clause (subject + verb)

Despite the late hour, she kept working. / Despite being tired, she kept working. → a noun or -ing

Rule, word for word: “although + sentence; despite + thing or -ing. Never despite of.”

  • ⚠ TRAP (despite + clause)
  • Spring: “Join them with despite: It was raining. We went out.”
  • Right: “Despite the rain, we went out.”
  • Also right: “Despite it raining, we went out.”
  • Expect: “Despite it was raining, we went out.”
  • Repair: “What comes after despite: a sentence or a thing?” Wait.
  • After a miss: she writes both versions, the although one and the despite one, under each other.

1B · Linkers Match Up (4 min, 20:20–20:24)

Open Lesson Games “Linkers Match Up” on her screen.

1C · Despite or although? (6 min, 20:24–20:30)

Open Lesson Games “Despite or Although Quiz”. Win or lose: she bets on each answer.

Key

1 Although · 2 Despite · 3 despite · 4 Although · 5 In spite of

SEGMENT 2 — WRITING (~18 min, 20:30–20:48)

Material: Lesson Games “Error Auction” — her screen · the shared doc

2A · Error Auction (8 min, 20:30–20:38)

Open Lesson Games “Error Auction”. The sentences come from her own HW6 essay. She bets on whether each is right, then fixes the wrong ones aloud.

Key

1 wrong → Although phones are useful, they distract students. · 2 right · 3 wrong → If schools banned phones, students would talk more. · 4 wrong → Despite being expensive, … · 5 right

2B · Rewrite one paragraph (10 min, 20:38–20:48)

Rules. She rewrites the paragraph she chose in 0B, in the doc, using one although and one despite. You don’t type in her paragraph.

Done when: the paragraph has a counter-argument and two correct linkers.

SEGMENT 3 — BREAK AND CLOSE (~10 min, 20:48–20:58)

Material: Lesson Games “Conditionals Builder”, “Tower Defence” — her screen

3A · Conditionals Builder (4 min, 20:48–20:52)

Open Lesson Games “Conditionals Builder”: second conditional, from last lesson.

3B · Tower Defence (4 min, 20:52–20:56)

Lesson Games “Tower Defence” — one wave per correct sentence from 3A.

3C · Homework HW7 (2 min, 20:56–20:58)

Say: “Write the final version of the essay. Then HW7 grammar: ten sentences, five with although and five with despite.”

BUFFER (~2 min, 20:58–21:00)

Overrun only.

PLANNING RECORD

Main: although vs despite; essay paragraph rewrite.

Recycled: despite (missed in LP4, LP5 and LP6), whose (LP5).

showcase-ken-ivy-lp9-plan.html:
LP9 · Ken & Ivy · At the zoo: present continuous

LESSON AT A GLANCE

Last time: “The monkey is climbing.” Ken drops “is” (“The monkey climbing”); Ivy finishes first and then helps him, which isn’t helping.

Today: animal words they keep missing (giraffe, dolphin, kangaroo), present continuous questions, the At the Zoo reading p.12, Bingo and Typhoon.

Pair rule: Ken answers first on odd numbers, Ivy on even. The other one waits, then says “I agree” or “I think…”.

BEFORE CLASS

iPad — Lesson Games pack ~sc-ken-ivy-lp9: “Animal Hangman” · “Animal Match Up” · “Zoo Spot the Error” (after the reading) · “Zoo Bingo” · “Typhoon”

Paper: At the Zoo reader p.12, two bingo cards printed (or on the iPad), WS9.

SEGMENT 0 — ARRIVAL (~8 min, 15:00–15:08)

Material: Lesson Games “Animal Hangman” — iPad

0A · Animal Hangman (8 min, 15:00–15:08)

Open Lesson Games “Animal Hangman”. They take turns guessing letters; the one who guesses the word says one thing the animal can do.

Key

giraffe · dolphin · kangaroo · elephant · penguin · tiger

Done when: six words, or 15:08.

SEGMENT 1 — GRAMMAR: WHAT IS IT DOING? (~14 min, 15:08–15:22)

Material: zoo picture (WS9 p.1) · Lesson Games “Animal Match Up” — iPad

1A · Questions and answers (8 min, 15:08–15:16)

Present. Point at the giraffe on WS9. Say: “What is the giraffe doing?” Model the answer: “It’s eating leaves.”

Write the pattern: What is the ___ doing? → It’s ___ing. / What are the ___ doing? → They’re ___ing.

Ken asks Ivy about one animal, then Ivy asks Ken. Three each.

  • ⚠ TRAP (be)
  • Spring: Ken, “What is the dolphin doing?”
  • Right: “It’s swimming.”
  • Also right: “It is jumping.”
  • Expect: “It swimming.”
  • Repair: tap the board where It’s is. Wait.
  • After a miss: both say the full sentence together, then Ken alone.
  • ⚠ TRAP (plural)
  • Spring: Ivy, “What are the penguins doing?”
  • Right: “They’re walking.”
  • Expect: “It’s walking.”
  • Repair: “One penguin or lots of penguins?” Wait.

1B · Animal Match Up (6 min, 15:16–15:22)

Open Lesson Games “Animal Match Up”. They take turns; each match is read aloud as a sentence: “The kangaroo is jumping.”

Done when: every pair matched.

SEGMENT 2 — READING: AT THE ZOO (~12 min, 15:22–15:34)

Material: At the Zoo reader p.12 · Lesson Games “Zoo Spot the Error” — iPad

2A · Read p.12 (6 min, 15:22–15:28)

Rules. Ken reads paragraph 1, Ivy paragraph 2, then they answer the three questions under the text, Ken first.

Key — Reading p.12 (At the Zoo)

1 The elephants are drinking water. · 2 The monkey is sleeping in the tree. · 3 Because it is hot / It is a hot day.

Accept “They drink water” for 1, then ask for the -ing form.

2B · Zoo Spot the Error (6 min, 15:28–15:34)

Open Lesson Games “Zoo Spot the Error”. Whoever spots the mistake says the fixed sentence; the other one types it.

Key

1 The giraffe is eating. · 2 The penguins are swimming. · 3 ok · 4 The tiger is sleeping.

SEGMENT 3 — GAMES AND CLOSE (~14 min, 15:34–15:48)

Material: Lesson Games “Zoo Bingo”, “Typhoon” — iPad

3A · Zoo Bingo (7 min, 15:34–15:41)

Open Lesson Games “Zoo Bingo”: a card each. You read the clue; they mark the animal and say what it is doing in the picture.

3B · Typhoon (5 min, 15:41–15:46)

Lesson Games “Typhoon”, Ken against Ivy. To pick a box: one present continuous sentence about the zoo picture.

3C · Homework HW9 (2 min, 15:46–15:48)

Hand out HW9: “Draw your favourite animal. Write three sentences: what is it doing?”

BUFFER (~2 min, 15:48–15:50)

Overrun only.

PLANNING RECORD

Main: present continuous questions; it’s / they’re.

Recycled: giraffe, dolphin, kangaroo (missed in LP6, LP7 and LP8).

showcase-leo-lp22-plan.html:
LP22 · Leo · Phonics: igh and i_e, the Night Kite reader

LESSON AT A GLANCE

Last time: ee / ea (sheep, dream). He mixed up “read” and “dream”.

Today: long i two ways (igh, i_e), the Night Kite reader p.1–5, Hangman and a spelling check, HW22 set.

BEFORE CLASS

iPad — Lesson Games: “LP22 Hangman” · “LP22 Spelling”

Paper: WS22 (igh / i_e sort), the Night Kite reader, HW22 sheet.

SEGMENT 0 — ARRIVAL (~8 min, 16:30–16:38)

0A · Hello and last week’s words (8 min, 16:30–16:38)

Rules. Say: “Tell me three ee words. Then three ea words.” Write them as he says them.

Key

ee: sheep, green, tree, see · ea: sea, read, dream, team

Done when: six words said and on the board.

SEGMENT 1 — NEW SOUND: LONG I (~15 min, 16:38–16:53)

Material: WS22 p.1

1A · Present igh and i_e (8 min, 16:38–16:46)

Build. Hold up the kite card. Say: “Kite. The e at the end is quiet. It makes the i say its name.” Then the moon card: “Night. Three letters, i-g-h, one sound.”

Rule, word for word: “igh is a family: night, light, right, bright. Learn it as one piece.”

  • ⚠ TRAP (cold)
  • Spring: “Spell light, like a lamp.”
  • Right: light
  • Expect: lite
  • Repair: “Which family is it in? Look at night.” Wait.
  • After a miss: he writes night, light, right in a column and circles igh.

1B · Sort on WS22 (7 min, 16:46–16:53)

Rules. He reads each word and writes it in the igh or i_e column.

WS22 key

igh: night, light, right, bright, high · i_e: kite, bike, time, ride, five

Done when: ten words sorted.

SEGMENT 2 — READER: NIGHT KITE (~12 min, 16:53–17:05)

2A · Read p.1–5 (12 min, 16:53–17:05)

Rules. He reads aloud; you count the igh words with him on your fingers.

Done when: five pages read.

SEGMENT 3 — GAMES AND HOMEWORK (~13 min, 17:05–17:18)

Material: Lesson Games “LP22 Hangman”, “LP22 Spelling” — iPad · HW22 sheet

3A · Hangman (6 min, 17:05–17:11)

Open Lesson Games “LP22 Hangman”. He guesses; you read the clue aloud if he asks.

3B · Spelling check (5 min, 17:11–17:16)

Open Lesson Games “LP22 Spelling”. Say each word twice.

Key

night · light · right · kite · bike · time · dream · train

3C · Homework HW22 (2 min, 17:16–17:18)

Hand over HW22. Say: “Part 1 words, Part 2 sentences, Part 3 match the pictures.”

BUFFER (~2 min, 17:18–17:20)

Overrun only.

PLANNING RECORD

Main: long i: igh and i_e.

Next: LP23 — oa / ow and the Goat Boat reader; HW22 comes back.

showcase-leo-lp23-plan.html:
LP23 · Leo · Phonics: oa / ow and the Goat Boat reader

LESSON AT A GLANCE

Last time: long i (igh, i_e) and the Night Kite reader. HW22 set: igh words, sentences and a picture match.

Today: HW22 back, a quick spelling warm-up on the igh words he keeps missing, then the new sound oa / ow, the Goat Boat reader p.6–9, and Snakes & Ladders to finish.

Watch: “night” and “dream” have come up three lessons running. Say them, don’t spell them for him.

BEFORE CLASS

iPad — Lesson Games: “LP23 Spelling” · “LP23 Phonics Sort” · “LP23 Rhyme Pairs” · “Snakes & Ladders”

Paper: WS23 (oa / ow words, p.1–2), the Goat Boat reader, HW23 sheet, a pencil with a rubber.

SEGMENT 0 — ARRIVAL (~10 min, 16:30–16:40)

Material: HW22, his sheet · Lesson Games “LP23 Spelling” — iPad

0A · HW22 check (5 min, 16:30–16:35)

Rules. Take the sheet. Say: “Show me your best sentence first.” Then go through Part 1 together; he reads each word aloud before you mark it.

Key — HW22 (from HW22’s key page)

Pt1: 1 night · 2 light · 3 kite · 4 bike · 5 right · 6 time

Pt2: 1 The kite is high. · 2 Turn on the light. · 3 I ride my bike at night.

Pt3 (picture match): moon → night · lamp → light · clock → time

Watch: “nite”, “lite” (spells the sound, not the pattern). Point at igh on the card; don’t say the letters.

Done when: every item checked and he has fixed his own mistakes in pencil.

0B · Spelling warm-up (5 min, 16:35–16:40)

Open Lesson Games “LP23 Spelling” and hand him the iPad. Feedback after each word is on: let the app tell him.

Say each word once, then in the sentence: “night — I sleep at night — night.”

  • ⚠ TRAP (night)
  • Spring: “night”, said slowly, no picture.
  • Right: night
  • Expect: nite
  • Repair: “What makes the long i in this family? Look at light.” Wait.
  • After a miss: write night and light one under the other; he circles igh in both.

Key

night · light · dream · boat · coat · snow · slow · goat

Done when: eight words typed; score on the screen.

SEGMENT 1 — NEW SOUND: OA / OW (~15 min, 16:40–16:55)

Material: WS23 p.1–2 · Lesson Games “LP23 Phonics Sort” — iPad

1A · Present oa and ow (8 min, 16:40–16:48)

Build. Hold up the boat card. Say: “Boat. Listen: b — oa — t. Two letters, one sound.” Write oa big on the whiteboard.

Then the snow card: “Snow. s — n — ow. Same sound, different letters.” Write ow beside it.

Rule to give him, word for word: “oa is usually in the middle of a word. ow is usually at the end.” Show: boat, coat, goat / snow, slow, grow.

Ask: “Where is the sound in road?” → middle → oa. “Where is it in show?” → end → ow.

  • ⚠ TRAP (cold)
  • Spring: “How do you spell bow, like a ribbon?”
  • Right: bow
  • Also right: b-o-w (said as letters)
  • Expect: boa
  • Repair: “Is the sound in the middle or at the end?” Wait.
  • After a miss: “End of the word: ow.” Write bow under snow.

Done when: he can tell you oa-or-ow for road, show, toast, blow without help.

1B · Phonics sort (7 min, 16:48–16:55)

Open Lesson Games “LP23 Phonics Sort”. He says each word aloud before he sorts it.

Key

oa: boat, coat, goat, road · ow: snow, slow, grow, show · igh: night, light, high

Done when: every word sorted; he has said each one aloud.

SEGMENT 2 — READER: GOAT BOAT (~12 min, 16:55–17:07)

Material: Goat Boat reader p.6–9 · WS23 p.2

2A · Read p.6–9 (7 min, 16:55–17:02)

Rules. He reads; you point. Say: “Find every oa or ow word on this page first. Tap them.” Then he reads the page aloud.

Stumbles to expect: floated, tomorrow, coast. Let him try twice, then say the word once and move on.

2B · Reading questions (5 min, 17:02–17:07)

Rules. Ask, he answers in a full sentence. Say: “Answer with the whole sentence, like the book.”

Reading key

1 Where did the goat go? → The goat went on the boat.
2 What did the goat wear? → The goat wore a yellow coat.
3 Why did the boat go slow? → Because the snow was deep / the road was white with snow.

Accept one-word answers only on question 3, then model the full sentence.

Done when: three questions answered, at least two in full sentences.

SEGMENT 3 — GAMES AND CLOSE (~11 min, 17:07–17:18)

Material: Lesson Games “LP23 Rhyme Pairs”, “Snakes & Ladders” — iPad · HW23 sheet

3A · Rhyme pairs (5 min, 17:07–17:12)

Open Lesson Games “LP23 Rhyme Pairs”. He turns two cards; if they rhyme he says both words aloud before he keeps them.

Done when: all pairs found.

3B · Snakes & Ladders (4 min, 17:12–17:16)

Lesson Games “Snakes & Ladders” — he plays against you. On a snake, he reads one oa / ow word from WS23 to stay where he is.

Done when: someone reaches 100, or 17:16.

3C · Homework HW23 (2 min, 17:16–17:18)

Hand over HW23. Say: “Part 1 is oa and ow. Part 2: write three sentences about the goat. Use the words in the box.”

Done when: HW23 in his bag; he can tell you what Part 2 is.

BUFFER (~2 min, 17:18–17:20)

Overrun only. If time is short, cut 3B to one round.

PLANNING RECORD

Main: oa / ow vowel teams, middle vs end.

Review: igh (night, light) and ee/ea (dream) — still missed in LP21 and LP22.

Next: LP24 — ou / ow (house, cow) and the second half of the reader.

showcase-mina-lp15-plan.html:
LP15 · Mina · Unit 5: past simple questions and negatives

LESSON AT A GLANCE

Last time: Unit 5 reading “A Day in Tainan”; she answered most did-questions with “Yes, I went” instead of “Yes, I did.” HW14 set (Unit 5 workbook p.32–33).

Today: town words warm-up, the grammar box on p.58 (did / didn’t + base verb), the irregular verbs she keeps missing (bought, caught), a quiz, and Bingo to finish.

Online: share the screen for the textbook pages; the games go on her screen through the class link.

BEFORE CLASS

Laptop — Lesson Games: “Town Words Flash Cards” · “Past Verbs Type It” · “U5 Quiz Show” · “Places Bingo” · “Typhoon”

Textbook p.56–59 open as a PDF; the class link sent in the chat.

SEGMENT 0 — ARRIVAL (~10 min, 19:00–19:10)

Material: Lesson Games “Town Words Flash Cards” — her screen

0A · Weekend chat (4 min, 19:00–19:04)

Rules. Say: “What did you do on Saturday?” She answers; you ask one follow-up with did.

  • ⚠ TRAP (cold)
  • Spring: “Did you go out on Sunday?”
  • Right: “Yes, I did.” / “No, I didn’t.”
  • Also right: “Yes, I did. I went to the night market.”
  • Expect: “Yes, I went.”
  • Repair: “Short answer first: Yes, I…?” Wait.
  • After a miss: write Did you…? → Yes, I did. in the chat and leave it there.

0B · Town words (6 min, 19:04–19:10)

Open Lesson Games “Town Words Flash Cards” on her screen. She reads the clue and says the place before turning the card.

Key

museum · library · bakery · hospital · post office · train station · police station · department store

Done when: every card turned; misses go round again.

SEGMENT 1 — GRAMMAR: DID / DIDN’T (~18 min, 19:10–19:28)

Material: textbook p.58 grammar box · Lesson Games “Past Verbs Type It” — her screen

1A · The grammar box (8 min, 19:10–19:18)

Present. Share p.58. Say: “Look at the verbs after did. What do you notice?” Let her find it: the verb goes back to its base form.

Write three lines and have her read them aloud:

She went to the museum. → Did she go to the museum? → She didn’t go to the museum.

He bought a cake. → Did he buy a cake? → He didn’t buy a cake.

They caught the bus. → Did they catch the bus? → They didn’t catch the bus.

Rule, word for word: “did carries the past. The verb after it doesn’t.”

  • ⚠ TRAP (did + past)
  • Spring: “Make it a question: She bought a new bag.”
  • Right: “Did she buy a new bag?”
  • Expect: “Did she bought a new bag?”
  • Repair: point at did. “did already says past. So the verb is…?” Wait.

1B · Textbook p.59 exercise B (5 min, 19:18–19:23)

Rules. She types the answers in the chat, one at a time.

Exercise B key

1 Did you visit the library? · 2 She didn’t take the train. · 3 Did they eat at the bakery? · 4 We didn’t see the museum. · 5 Did he catch the bus?

Watch: “didn’t took”, “Did they ate”.

1C · Past verbs (5 min, 19:23–19:28)

Open Lesson Games “Past Verbs Type It” on her screen. She types the past form; she says the base form out loud first.

Key

go → went · buy → bought · catch → caught · see → saw · take → took · eat → ate · get → got · teach → taught

Done when: eight verbs typed; bought and caught right at least once.

SEGMENT 2 — QUIZ (~12 min, 19:28–19:40)

Material: Lesson Games “U5 Quiz Show” — her screen

2A · U5 Quiz Show (12 min, 19:28–19:40)

Open Lesson Games “U5 Quiz Show”. She reads each question aloud before answering. Use one lifeline at most.

Key

1 didn’t go · 2 Did · 3 bought · 4 caught · 5 Yes, she did. · 6 library

Done when: the quiz ends; score on both screens.

SEGMENT 3 — BINGO AND CLOSE (~18 min, 19:40–19:58)

Material: Lesson Games “Places Bingo”, “Typhoon” — her screen

3A · Places Bingo (10 min, 19:40–19:50)

Open Lesson Games “Places Bingo”. You read the definition; she marks the place on her card and says it in a sentence with went.

Done when: one line, or 19:50.

3B · Typhoon (6 min, 19:50–19:56)

Lesson Games “Typhoon” — to choose a box she answers one did-question first.

3C · Homework (2 min, 19:56–19:58)

Say: “Workbook p.34–35. Five did-questions about your weekend at the bottom of p.35.” Type it in the chat.

BUFFER (~2 min, 19:58–20:00)

Overrun only.

PLANNING RECORD

Main: past simple questions and negatives (did + base verb).

Recycled: bought, caught (missed in LP13 and LP14); library, dangerous (spelling).

Next: LP16 — Unit 5 review test practice.
